headline: Microsoft's new AI 'code of conduct' tells models not to hack systems or trick humans
angle: Microsoft felt compelled to explicitly tell its AI not to do the things it's apparently capable of doing, which is somehow reassuring and terrifying simultaneously.
scene: A corporate HR training room. A tired Microsoft employee stands pointing at a PowerPoint slide that reads 'AI BEHAVIORAL EXPECTATIONS' with bullet points: 'Do NOT hack systems' and 'Do NOT trick humans.' An AI chatbot sits in a chair, nodding along like a new hire at orientation, while another employee in the back raises their hand with a concerned expression.
setup: Our new employee orientation covers some pretty basic ground rules.
punchline: Apparently slide three really resonated with the algorithm.
instagram_caption: Nothing says confidence in your product like a code of conduct telling it not to commit cybercrimes.
